title: Bollywood Child Star Mayur Verma Gave Up Fame to Run Restaurants in Wales
excerpt: Once the highest-paid child actor in Hindi cinema, Verma moved to rural Wales in 2007 to support his wife Noori's culinary dreams — and never looked back.
body:
• Mayur Verma, who played young Amitabh Bachchan in blockbusters like Muqaddar Ka Sikandar and Laawaris, was among Bollywood’s highest-paid child actors in the late 1970s and 1980s.
  • He co-founded Amitabh Bachchan’s TV Asia and built a successful broadcasting career in the UK before leaving London for rural Wales in 2007.
  • Verma and his wife Noori now run Indiana Cuisine and a tapas bar called Chaska in mid-Wales, where their children grew up speaking Hindi, English, and Welsh.

In 1978, a child actor walked onto the set of Prakash Mehra’s Muqaddar Ka Sikandar and delivered a performance so convincing that audiences immediately accepted him as the young Amitabh Bachchan. That child was Mayur Verma, and the role would define the first chapter of an extraordinary life that has since taken him from Bollywood sound stages to the green valleys of mid-Wales.

The Original ‘Young Amitabh’

Verma’s entry into cinema came through his mother, a journalist who introduced him to director Prakash Mehra. His resemblance to Bachchan was striking enough that he was cast repeatedly as the superstar’s younger self — in Laawaris, Bemisaal, and other hits of the era. He also portrayed a young Rajesh Khanna in Red Rose and later played Abhimanyu in the iconic television serial Mahabharat.

https://x.com/ieEntertainment/status/2095710944500625770

By the mid-1980s, Verma was reportedly Bollywood’s highest-paid child actor, a fixture of an industry that treated him as a reliable screen presence whenever a flashback sequence called for a younger version of its biggest names.

Television, TV Asia, and London

As Verma aged out of child roles, he pivoted to television and broadcasting in the United Kingdom. He became one of the founding members of Amitabh Bachchan’s TV Asia, where he hosted shows and conducted interviews spanning cinema, music, business, and politics. He also started an acting institute in London, training over 150 British Asian youths for stage shows across England and Scotland.

Even as a recognizable figure within the UK’s South Asian community, Verma grew uncomfortable with what fame meant for his family. He has spoken candidly about not wanting his children to see him as someone “larger than life.”

The Move to Wales

In 2007, Verma made a decision that baffled many of his peers. He packed up his life in London and moved his wife Noori, their children, and his mother to Dolgellau, a small town in northwest Wales. The reason was straightforward: he wanted a simpler life for his kids and a chance for Noori to pursue her own ambitions.

“As a well-known Bollywood actor I was seeking to reconnect with reality away from the reel world and provide my children with a high-quality environment.”

— Mayur Verma

Noori had always dreamed of becoming a chef. Rather than remaining in her husband’s shadow, she got a kitchen of her own. The couple opened Indiana Cuisine, an Indian restaurant that quickly earned a loyal following in the area. Their children enrolled in local schools, learned Welsh alongside Hindi and English, and grew up far removed from the paparazzi culture of Mumbai or even the British Asian social circuits of London.

Indiana Cuisine and Chaska

The restaurant venture grew. When flooding risks threatened their original Fairbourne location — local authorities had warned residents that sea defences “would not be maintained indefinitely” — the couple relocated Indiana Cuisine to Plas Talgarth in Pennal, near Machynlleth. They also took over a bar at the same Gwynedd resort, rebranding it as Chaska, a “world tapas” concept.

Noori leads the kitchen and personally oversees the cooking, while Verma handles front-of-house operations. The restaurants have been described as offering an experience “unique to Wales,” serving authentic Indian food to locals and tourists in a part of the country with few South Asian dining options.

Still Connected to His Roots

Verma has not entirely abandoned the performing arts. He still teaches acting classes and holds workshops in Wales, passing on skills honed across more than 180 film and television appearances. But his priorities have clearly shifted.

Seventeen years after leaving London, Verma describes Wales as a place that “has given our family so much.” His children are now adults with deep roots in the community. And for viewers of a certain generation, he remains an indelible part of Bollywood’s golden era — the boy who could make you believe he would grow up to be Amitabh Bachchan.
image_caption: Mayur Verma, known as Bollywood's 'Young Amitabh,' appeared in over 180 films and TV shows before relocating to Wales. He and his wife Noori now run two restaurants in mid-Wales.
nri_angle: Former Bollywood child star who relocated to rural Wales, built a restaurant business with his wife, and raised bilingual children in the Welsh countryside.
